summary: Bounded read-only Observer state reads during atomic publication, without relaxing private-file safety or inventing source freshness.
origin: The P3E13 sanitizer aggregate found state-unsafe in the unchanged Observer dev.18 watch/status test. A normal atomic rename can leave an already opened old file with link count zero. Checking descriptor permissions before classifying metadata change misidentifies that publication race as unsafe input.

policy.read: Validate the named file first, then compare its full stamp with the opened descriptor before interpreting changed descriptor permissions/link count. A changed stamp is state-changed, never proof that the replacement is safe.
policy.retry: StateStore::load performs at most three complete read attempts, and only retries state-changed/file-changed. Each attempt rechecks directory identity, named file privacy, descriptor identity, bounded content, final stamps and JSON validity. Exhaustion returns state-changed; no unbounded loop or sleep.
policy.unsafe: A stable symlink, hard link, wrong owner/mode, oversized or malformed file still fails. The reader never accepts an unsafe replacement, returns partial JSON, repairs pending state, writes a file, obtains the writer lock or validates live project sources.
policy.scope: No new configuration or persisted-state format. Server, Core and global stable delivery are unchanged by this Observer correction.

sources.use: POSIX rename removes the replaced link while open file references can remain alive; zero-link descriptors are a possible publication interleaving.
